The hidden cost of hand soldering

Hand soldering is where THT quality quietly leaks away

Every joint soldered by hand is a lottery ticket. The same solder, the same iron, different hands — and the defects only show up at test.

Hand soldering is a lottery

Tip angle, dwell time and feed rate drift with every operator and every hour. Quality follows mood, not a recipe.

Cold joints and bridges

Insufficient heat makes dull, grainy joints; excess heat bridges adjacent pads. Both are invisible until electrical test.

Tip temperature guesswork

Manual irons cool under load. Operators compensate by pressing harder or waiting — and the solder quality pays for it.

Training and turnover

A good solderer takes months to train and leaves for a dollar more. The skill walks out the door.

Wire and tip waste

Solder wire is overfed by hand, tips are burned by over-temperature, and scrap joins the rework pile.

Throughput capped by hands

Output scales with headcount, and headcount is getting harder to find — the soldering bench sets the pace.

Equipment options

Configure the robot to your soldering work

Every configuration below is available on the desktop solder robot family. We recommend a starting configuration after reviewing your boards and soldering points.

Single head / dual head

Choose one head for simple boards or two heads for double throughput on high-volume joints.

Single / dual / back-to-back

Dual tables let the operator load while the robot solders; back-to-back runs two processes on one frame.

Open frame / protective cover

Protective cover models add operator safety and fume containment for stricter factories.

Stepper / servo

Stepper is cost-effective for standard joints; servo adds precision for fine-pitch and dense work.

Solder breaker + cleaning box

The solder breaker cracks oxidized wire; the cleaning box keeps the tip tinned and oxide-free.

Tips, fixtures, R-axis

Custom tips and PCB fixtures designed from your samples; rotatable head for angled joints.

Installation guide

From bench to production in five steps

Installation is simple enough for one technician in a day — and we include free installation and training with every machine.

01 · Bench & fixture

Place the robot on a stable workbench. We design the PCB fixture to your boards — panel size, support points and clearance for the tip.

02 · Utilities

Connect 220 V mains power (full-voltage AC110–220 V on the S-HX331R). No compressed air is required for standard operation; prepare soldering wire and tips.

03 · Programming

Set soldering temperature (0–500 °C), teach paths with the handheld teaching box, and store programs — capacity for more than 100 sets.

04 · Trial run

Solder sample boards, then tune temperature, feed speed and tip height until every joint passes your acceptance criteria.

05 · Training & ramp

Free installation and operator training included; 24/7 worldwide support and 1-day spare-part lead time after handover.

Buyer's FAQ

Questions buyers ask before choosing a solder robot

What can a desktop solder robot replace?

A single robot replaces at least three manual soldering stations — the S-HX331R verifies 1 robot ≥ 3 workers. The robot handles spot soldering, drag soldering and rotary soldering on ICs, PCBs, LCDs, relays, loudspeakers, USB connectors, LED strips, terminals and automotive parts.

Which robot should I choose: S-C5331R or S-HX331R?

Choose the S-C5331R dual-table robot when you have a steady volume of the same board and want the highest output per station — two tables run in one cycle. Choose the S-HX331R four-axis rotary robot when joints need angled or rotary access, higher speed (0–800 mm/s) or external RS232 control. Send your boards and we recommend the configuration.

How is a new product programmed?

With the handheld teaching box: set the soldering temperature (0–500 °C), teach the solder path point by point, and store the program. Capacity is over 100 sets on the S-HX331R with 3-axis interpolation.

What utilities does a solder robot need?

220 V mains power (full-voltage AC110–220 V on the S-HX331R). No compressed air is required for standard operation. Prepare soldering wire, tips and a stable workbench with your PCB fixture.

What is the defect rate?

On the S-HX331R the verified reject ratio is ≤ 2‰. Because temperature is controlled to ±2 °C and the tip returns to set point quickly, cold joints and over-burn — the two most common hand-soldering defects — are eliminated at the source.

How do I get a quote and ROI estimate?

Email info@smthelp.com or WhatsApp +86 136 0256 2576 with your board samples or drawings, joint count per board and monthly volume. We reply with a robot recommendation, configuration, quotation and ROI estimate — typically within 24 hours.
